description:
Music for Digital Burnout | Surbahar Instrumental | 1.5 Hours

Can't stop scrolling? Fried by the feed? A full day of screens, notifications and doomscrolling leaves you wired but exhausted — burned out by digital noise, mind still buzzing long after you put the phone down.

Start here. Ninety minutes of slow, deep surbahar — the bass cousin of the sitar — to help you unplug and let an overstimulated, burned-out mind recover. Long resonant notes, wide space, nothing to look at. Close the eyes and let the digital noise drain out.

What you'll hear: deep, warm string tones in Raga Bageshri — soothing late-evening character, unhurried, with long sustains and quiet pauses. No glare, no busy rhythm. Just slowness and space to recover.

Best for: recovering from a day of screens · putting the phone down for the night · resting a wired, overstimulated mind · a phone-free wind-down · a dark room and headphones.

🔔 Subscribe to Raga Focus for Indian instrumental music to recover from digital burnout, unplug from the feed, and let an overstimulated mind come down.
thumbnail_prompt: Pichwai/Kangra miniature painting style, ornate warm-gold patterned border. EVENING palette — deep teal, indigo, aged-cream parchment, low warm lantern glow, the world gone dark and quiet (the opposite of a glowing screen). Central figure: a still, composed musician with a surbahar (large deep sitar), eyes closed, seated calm in low evening light — the posture of someone who has finally put the screens away. Mood = relief, dark quiet, the glare gone. Visually distinct from the channel's bright/morning thumbnails. Overlay text 'CAN'T STOP SCROLLING?' in dark-teal serif, large and mobile-readable (pain/behavior Q-hook for the digital-burnout lane). Mobile-first: minimal clutter, high overlay contrast.
suno_prompt_A: Slow deep Indian surbahar (bass sitar), Raga Bageshri — soothing late-evening introspective character, the feeling of unplugging from a day of screens and letting a wired, burned-out, overstimulated mind slowly recover, deep resonant plucked string tones with long meend glissando slides and gamak ornamentation and long restful pauses, soft tanpura drone underneath, no percussion, no tabla, 432Hz tuning, 52 BPM, low register, warm intimate spacious production, the deep string entering clearly within the first few seconds (no long silent build), seamless loop-friendly texture, like dark quiet replacing screen glare, deeply unwinding not drowsy, no vocals, no humming, no human voice
suno_prompt_B: Instrumental only, no vocals, no humming, no tabla, no percussion, slow deep surbahar bass sitar, Raga Bageshri — soothing late-evening introspective, deep resonant plucked tones with long meend slides, gamak, and long pauses, soft tanpura drone, 432Hz, 52 BPM, low register, warm spacious intimate production, deep string enters within first few seconds (no silent build), seamless loop, like unplugging and letting a burned-out mind recover, unwinding not drowsy

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: Surbahar-ONLY (no tabla, no percussion). Deep low register, slow 52 BPM but NOT sleep-drowsy — Theta 6Hz = deep relaxation for a wired, burned-out mind. Raga Bageshri's soothing late-evening character fits burnout recovery / unplug. CANNIBAL-SAFEGUARD: must sound distinct from the owned 'Deep Rest Surbahar' hero — frame as recovering/unplugging from digital overstimulation, not passive deep-rest. Deep string should enter within the first few seconds (hook) — avoid a long silent tanpura-only intro.
